summary: Regression run of L1-L5 Network Cap Cascade after mining.py fix. All 10/10 pytest tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_l1l5_network_cap_cascade.py. The mining.calculate_mining_rate now derives direct_referrals from level_counts['l1'] (BFS helper) — unifying the source-of-truth with growth_economy. Mixed-flavour test (1 L1 via uid + 1 L1 via referral_code) now correctly returns direct_referrals=2 and network_cap=832 (800 + 16*2). Consistency test confirms mining and growth endpoints return identical L1 counts. Sanity check on live API for Suresh (Elite, no referrals) returns expected network_cap=800, formula string matches locked formula, and l3/l4/l5 all 0.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix verified: /app/backend/routes/mining.py line ~355 now uses direct_referrals = level_counts.get('l1', 0) from the BFS helper (get_downline_level_counts) — single source-of-truth, handles mixed uid/referral_code parents correctly, and saves one DB query. Previous duplicate count_documents call has been removed cleanly.

Cleanup verified: dead helpers (get_network_size, get_l1_indirect_count) and NETWORK_CAP_DIRECT_MAX constant are no longer referenced; 8 stale referral test files deleted. Backend module loads clean with no import errors and live API returns the canonical formula string.

No residue confirmed in DB (7 real users intact).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature is fully verified end-to-end. mining.py and growth_economy.py now use the same BFS-based L1 count via get_downline_level_counts, eliminating the inconsistency reported in iteration_233. Canonical formula min(8000, 800 + 16*L1 + 5*L2 + 3*L3 + 2*L4 + 1*L5) verified across /api/mining/rate-breakdown, /api/mining/status, /api/growth/network-stats, and /api/notifications/referrals/{uid}/level-breakdown. Re-run pytest backend/tests/test_l1l5_network_cap_cascade.py -v anytime to revalidate.
rca of the issue: Original RCA (from iteration_233): mining.py had a separate db.users.count_documents({'referred_by': user_id}) call that only matched uid, while growth_economy used $or [uid, referral_code]. Fix applied: mining.calculate_mining_rate now reads direct_referrals from level_counts['l1'] returned by the shared BFS helper. Verified by TestMixedFlavourReferral.test_mining_rate_breakdown_mixed_flavour_bug (PASSED with direct_referrals==2) and TestMixedFlavourReferral.test_mining_and_growth_direct_referrals_consistency (PASSED — both endpoints return identical L1 counts).
